name: Literature review outline
pitch: Creates a structured outline from ten research papers, ready to review or edit.
instructions: Read the ten papers listed in the folder. Summarise each paper in one sentence that states its main claim or finding. Group the summaries by theme or method that emerges across the papers. Write a top‑level outline with an introduction, the grouped themes as sections, and a conclusion. Format the outline in Markdown with headings and bullet points. If any paper cannot be opened or read, note that its content could not be checked and continue with the others. When finished, present the Markdown outline to the person and ask if they would like to add, remove, or reorder any sections.

examples.does: reads the papers, groups them by theme, and writes a Markdown outline

skills.name: summarise-and-group-papers
skills.description: Turn ten research papers into a themed outline.
skills.body: 1. List the file names of the ten papers in the workspace. 2. Open each file and read its abstract or introduction. 3. Write one sentence summarising the main claim or finding of each paper. 4. Read all summaries and identify common themes, methods, or gaps. 5. Arrange the themes into a logical order for a literature review. 6. Draft a Markdown outline with an introduction, a heading for each theme, and bullet points containing the paper summaries under the relevant theme. 7. Add a conclusion section that synthesises the overall state of the field. 8. If a paper cannot be read, add a note: "[Content of [filename] could not be checked]." 9. Return the completed Markdown outline to the person.

readme:
# Literature review outline

Creates a Markdown outline from ten research papers, grouping them by theme or method. 

**What it needs:** access to the ten paper files in the workspace. 

**What it will not do:** it does not argue a position or cite sources beyond the summaries it produces.
